clue.text: Item given to daughter training as solicitor

parts.note: an item in a list or contract is an article
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: Something is handed to a daughter who is studying to become a solicitor.
explanation.walkthrough: An ARTICLED clerk in Britain is a trainee solicitor bound by articles (a training contract) to a firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Trainee lawyers were bound to a firm by articles of clerkship, so a trainee was described as articled.

clue.text: Retreat, without defeat perhaps?

explanation.surface: Someone backs off, wondering whether that counts as avoiding a loss.
explanation.walkthrough: Split it as WITH DRAW: a game ending with a draw is one finished without defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull back is a synonym for retreat, and a match that ends with a draw has no loser, hence no defeat.

clue.text: Suggest work in plain English

indicators.note: in places the word for work inside the word for plain English

parts.note: prose is ordinary, unversed language
OP is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: An instruction to put forward some work written in simple language.
explanation.definitionFit: To put forward an idea is a synonym of suggest.

clue.text: Typical assumption in Kyoto

parts.note: assumption here means the act of putting on clothing, so this is the garment a person in Japan traditionally dons

explanation.surface: A remark about what people in Kyoto usually take for granted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Assumption' reads as a belief, but it is used in its sense of putting on a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: The traditional wide-sleeved robe of Japan is the garment typically put on there.

clue.text: Have chief job in school to execute

explanation.surface: A headteacher appointed to carry out a plan.
explanation.walkthrough: Split it as BE HEAD: to be the head of a school is to have its chief job.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting off someone's head is a method of execution, and being the head teacher is the top school job.

clue.text: Trying to take a message, one'll get in a flap

definitions.text: Trying to take a message, one'll get in a flap

parts.words: Trying to take a message, one'll get in a flap
parts.note: reads as a flustered office worker, but describes a bird that carries notes and flaps its wings to fly

explanation.surface: A harassed person panics while attempting to note down a phone message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get in a flap' sounds like panicking; here it means literally flapping wings in flight.
explanation.definitionFit: Homing birds were trained to fly notes back to their loft, flapping all the way.

clue.text: Working against bar, giving performance

parts.note: a counter is the bar over which drinks or goods are served
acting is a stage performance

explanation.surface: Someone at a bar puts on a show while opposing something.
explanation.definitionFit: To neutralise or oppose an effect is to work against it.

clue.text: Preservation society getting everyone's confidence?

explanation.surface: A heritage charity wins the faith of the whole country.
explanation.walkthrough: The NATIONAL TRUST is the British charity that preserves historic houses and countryside; read literally it is the trust of the nation.
explanation.definitionFit: The British heritage charity conserves stately homes, and a whole country's faith is literally its national trust.

clue.text: In German city, do some eating around one

indicators.note: around places the word for eating so it encloses the numeral for one

parts.note: to munch is to chew food
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An invitation to have a snack somewhere in Germany at about one o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bavarian capital is a major city of Germany.

clue.text: Characteristic actor probably needs on stage

explanation.surface: A remark on what a typical performer requires in a theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: A theatrical prop is short for property, an object an actor handles on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A quality or attribute of something is one of its features, and stage objects are formally theatrical items called props.

clue.text: Pair party round university

indicators.note: round makes the word for party wrap about the letter for university

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: Two people throw a party near a university campus.
explanation.definitionFit: Two performers working together form a twosome.

clue.text: Less fresh way Lear may be produced

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

indicators.note: produced suggests the name Lear is reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A comment on how a production of King Lear might seem tired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May be produced' reads as staging Shakespeare's King Lear, but it is the anagram signal working on the name alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread or news that is older and less fresh is described comparatively as more stale.

clue.text: Wintry fall, but sign of spring?

explanation.surface: A wintry snowfall that also hints that the warmer season is near.
explanation.definitionFit: A fall of snow can be called a snow drop, and the white flower blooms as one of the earliest signs of spring.

clue.text: Wife, these days, has a lot of cash

parts.note: AD (anno Domini) marks the present era

explanation.surface: Nowadays a wife has plenty of money.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick roll of banknotes signifies a large amount of money.

clue.text: Dispute about notice — one could be boring

indicators.note: about makes the word for dispute go round the word for notice

parts.note: a brawl is a noisy quarrel
an ad is a notice or advertisement

explanation.surface: An argument over an announcement that may turn out dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' seems to mean dull, but a bradawl is a tool for boring holes.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpenter's small pointed tool punches holes, so it is used for boring.

clue.text: A pet's not good? Bother!

indicators.note: not tells us the letter for good is missing

parts.note: a dog is a typical pet; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in exasperation that their pet is misbehaving.
explanation.definitionFit: Fuss or trouble is a sense of bother, as in much ado about nothing.

clue.text: Doctors' exam the most ignorant could pass

definitions.text: Doctors' exam the most ignorant could pass

parts.words: Doctors' exam the most ignorant could pass
parts.note: the exam is given by doctors, testing health rather than knowledge, so even someone uneducated could pass it

explanation.surface: A jibe that medical qualifying exams are so easy anyone could pass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctors' exam' seems to be a test that doctors sit; it is one they give to patients.
explanation.definitionFit: A physical health check carried out by a doctor is a medical examination.

clue.text: It indicates when to fill your breakfast cup

definitions.text: It indicates when to fill your breakfast cup

parts.words: It indicates when to fill your breakfast cup
parts.note: the cup is an egg cup, filled once a small sandglass shows the boiling time is up

explanation.surface: A gadget that tells you when to pour your morning tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breakfast cup' suggests tea or coffee; it is the cup that holds a boiled egg.
explanation.definitionFit: A small sandglass times a boiled egg, so it signals when the egg is ready to serve.

clue.text: I told ray off for heathen behaviour

indicators.note: off suggests the words are spoiled or out of order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone scolded a man named Ray for pagan conduct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off' looks like part of 'told off' (scolded), but it is the anagram signal on I TOLD RAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Worshipping images or false gods is behaviour Christians historically called heathen.

clue.text: Agreed to differ about new explosive

indicators.note: about places the rearranged letters around the letter for new
differ suggests the word agreed is changed into another order

explanation.surface: Two sides concede disagreement over a novel bomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To differ' rearranges AGREED as GREADE, which goes 'about' N.
explanation.definitionFit: A small bomb thrown by hand is an explosive weapon.

clue.text: Ship carrying sherry

explanation.surface: A sailing vessel with a cargo of fortified wine.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a schooner is also a large sherry glass.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-masted sailing vessel is one sense; a tall glass that holds a measure of fortified wine is the other.

clue.text: Lass I love coming up to north sea base

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: a lass is a girl
O is love, a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: A girl and her love sail up to the North Sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming up' turns the whole run GIRLIO, giving the answer read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An offshore drilling platform serves as a base for extracting petroleum at sea.

clue.text: Mean to hold court, offering divine drink

indicators.note: to hold makes the word for mean enclose the abbreviation for court

parts.note: near is an old word for stingy or mean

explanation.surface: A stingy host holds court while serving a heavenly beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' seems to be a verb; it is the adjective, as in stingy.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the gods drank this, so it is the drink of the divine.

clue.text: Crossing river, reached ornamental cave

indicators.note: crossing puts the word for reached across, around, the letter for river

parts.note: got to means reached

explanation.surface: After crossing a river, explorers arrived at a decorative cavern.
explanation.definitionFit: A decorative artificial cavern in a garden is a classic folly feature.

clue.text: Consume flesh, tearing off head

indicators.note: removing the head takes away the first letter of the word for flesh

parts.note: meat is animal flesh

explanation.surface: A predator devours flesh, ripping off its victim's head.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat food is to consume it.

clue.text: Will start to cook with an open-air boiler

parts.note: Billy is a pet form of William, as is Will

indicators.note: start to takes only the first letter of cook

explanation.surface: A man named Will begins cooking using an outdoor kettle.
explanation.walkthrough: A BILLYCAN is the tin pot campers in Australia boil water in over a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal campfire pot is used for boiling water outdoors.

clue.text: One taking vehicle to America? He flew

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a car is a vehicle
US is the United States

explanation.surface: Someone driving to America wonders who flew there.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Icarus flew on wax wings too near the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical son of Daedalus took to the air on wings of feathers and wax.

clue.text: Unsympathetic advice to woman in labour?

definitions.text: Unsympathetic advice to woman in labour?

parts.words: Unsympathetic advice to woman in labour?
parts.note: the stock advice to endure stoically is read with bear in its sense of giving birth

explanation.surface: A heartless remark to a mother-to-be in the delivery room.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom means put up with it cheerfully; the joke is that bear also means give birth.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means put up with hardship with a smile, unsympathetic counsel to someone in pain.
